feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 2 (16 mm footprint, x = ±0.03 m, kp 2.5, kd 0.2) still logged one line-loss event on the oval and S-bend and ended every run off_track at max_error about 0.0605 m, so the footprint alone did not remove loss. Iteration 1 (12 mm, same span) logged 2 losses on the oval, and its kp 3.0 raised steering_oscillation to 0.186. Span is the lever the evidence points to: the centre sensors detect the tape to about 0.0205 m offset, and the outer sensors at ±0.03 m stop at about 0.0505 m, just inside the 0.06 m limit. Widening to ±0.05 m is the proposed test. After the next race, decide as follows. If line_loss_events is still above zero on the oval or S-bend at ±0.05 m, the loss is not geometric: check the controller's line_loss handling and the start position before changing geometry. If line_loss_events is zero but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, reduce mass to 0.6 kg, because body_width cannot move the off-track limit. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
requested_changes: Keep the seven sensors at x = ±0.05 m (outer) with 16 mm footprints at y = 0.04 m. Iteration 2 showed ±0.03 m leaves a line-loss event, and the threshold model says ±0.05 m moves the loss radius beyond the 0.06 m limit.

If line_loss_events is zero but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, reduce mass to 0.6 kg rather than changing body_width. Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.068 m with no clean recovery, and body_width cannot raise the limit above 0.06 m.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed, since base_speed has been held at 1.3 and speed headroom is untested.
